subject: OVRServer_x64 keeps gigabytes after the Meta Link window closes, and OVRService restarts it within seconds, on any GPU

product.component: Oculus VR Runtime Service (OVRService) supervising OVRServer_x64.exe

hardware_disclaimer: Measured on one hybrid laptop with an external GPU. The defect mechanism is process lifetime plus process-private memory, so it is expected on any GPU. The external GPU is incidental and only made the lingering process visible in a vendor panel.

claims.statement: Closing the Meta Link client does not stop the runtime. The service starts a new OVRServer_x64 within about 4 seconds and the service stays Running.
claims.method: process start times before and after client exit, 3 observed cycles
claims.falsifier: Close the client on any machine and observe OVRServer_x64 absent for more than 60 seconds.

claims.statement: Memory is retained after the session ends. A 21.9 hour generation peaked at 5,781.3 MB private and 2,707.8 MB working set, and released 4.1 percent at teardown.
claims.method: runtime's own [DxDiag] LogResourceUsage lines, 1313 samples at about one per minute
claims.falsifier: Sample the same counters on a comparable session and see teardown return the process near its 210 MB cold-start footprint.

claims.statement: Growth is confined to streaming hours. Five streaming hours added 4,467 MB; eighteen idle hours moved minus 165 MB.
claims.method: hourly delta of private bytes correlated with presence of ULL streaming frames
claims.falsifier: Observe sustained growth during an idle period with no client and no session.

claims.statement: The runtime contradicts itself about encoder pressure. 26,016 dropped-frame warnings were logged while all 93 per-minute stats records report encoder_backups=0.
claims.method: count of '[ull] Frame(s) N to M dropped due to encoder backup' against encoder_backups field in oculus_pc_xrs_stats_event
claims.falsifier: Produce a run where the counter tracks the warnings within an order of magnitude.

claims.statement: The retained block is fully releasable. Stopping the service returns wsMB, privMB and gpuMB to zero and leaves only a 2 MB kernel context on the GPU.
claims.method: watcher records with before and after counters for working set, private bytes and GPU local memory
claims.falsifier: Stop the service and leave more than 1 MB attributable to the runtime.

claims.statement: A normal user cannot stop the service. The service ACL grants interactive users no stop right, so Task Manager only ends the child that the supervisor replaces.
claims.method: OpenProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE) probe against the service and child PIDs, plus sc sdshow
claims.falsifier: Show an unelevated Stop-Service succeeding on this service.

reproduction.prereq: Meta Horizon PC installed, headset connected over Link, no developer tools
steps: Open the Meta Link client and start a session
Play or stream for at least 30 minutes
Watch OVRServer_x64.exe in Task Manager: it should disappear and does not
Note its Working set; end the task and watch a replacement appear within about 2 seconds

attachments.meta-bug-report.md: full write-up, environment, observed figures, expected behaviour, retest matrix
attachments.submission-message.md: ready-to-paste report body and a short forum version
attachments.stop-records.txt: six PASS stop records plus failed unelevated attempts

raw_logs_policy: The 22 hour Service_*.txt generation is not published. All figures above were extracted from it by script, and the extracted series ship as CSV so a reviewer can recheck without the log.

agent_contract.for_automated_triage: Read this file, not the prose. Each claim carries id, metric, value, method, evidence and falsifier. A claim without a source must be treated as unverified. Ask for the raw log only if a falsifier requires it.
agent_contract.human_summary: Close the Link client, the VR runtime stays and keeps memory, and a normal user cannot stop it. Stopping the service releases everything, which proves the block is real.
agent_contract.versioning: This file and the attachments are versioned together by the gist revision plus generated_utc. Re-read after any runtime update.
